summary:
I reconciled the tree with design 10 (the narrowed slice) and with the critique's decisions F1–F5.

**Core:**
- The precaution list is now `KnownWorkarounds`, with the single entry `wcifs-layer-store`.
- Scans take the switched-on ids from `ScanOptions.EnabledWorkarounds`.
- `ContainerLayerStore` is the only code that reads the switch, and it decides only the exclusion of the store. A picked root at or inside the store is refused whatever the switch says (F1).
- Scan results now carry the precaution's id, so the window words its notices without naming the entry.

**App:**
- A Settings window lists every precaution generically. Turning one off goes through a WPF confirmation window, which the startup hook can answer.
- The refusal and not-scanned notices name the defect, wcifs.sys, and the Settings checkbox.
- The report's `precautions` field becomes `workarounds`; `core.notScanned` is added.

**Test rigs:**
- `PoolWatch.ps1` is rewritten lean. It writes a plan line and marks for each arm, kills an arm when the guard trips (6 GiB of pool over that arm's own start, or under 3 GiB available), and records an arm not started because the guard was already tripped as a cascade. `-Report` prints RUN COMPLETE or RUN INCOMPLETE and raw nets, never a verdict. `-Rehearse` runs the same protocol on a generated tree.
- ScanArm and the old verdict tests are deleted. `PoolWatchCases.ps1` now holds the PoolWatch cases.
- The hook gained a `settings` mode, driven by window case X-005. Window case X-006 checks the notices.

**Rules and record:**
- The four new rules have plants that must fire and correct lines that must stay quiet. The two old plants that pointed into ScanArm were moved.
- The design record is rewritten: the tag table, the measured restart reclaim, spike #87's evidence that arm L passed the store (L.json and a folder count copied in), the 6 GiB arithmetic, and the hand-off of every judgement to SC-128.

**Results:**
- The planted-store tests (32), the repro, window cases X-005 and X-006, the five PoolWatch cases (including a full rehearsal reading RUN COMPLETE), all 11 window mutants and the rules harness (93 of 93 rows as recorded) pass.
- The full suite gives 532 passed and the same 3 last-access failures the slice started with.

files.why: Design 10's single list of precautions against outside defects, with Id, Title, Defect, WhereItLives, Precaution, IfTurnedOff and DefaultOn. Its first entry is 'wcifs-layer-store'. The text never promises that a picked root inside the store will be scanned (F1). DefaultEnabled and Find are included.
Replaced by KnownWorkarounds, under the design's name and id. WorkaroundSwitches is replaced by an IReadOnlySet of enabled ids.

This is now the one place the switch is read, and it governs only Exclude: with the workaround off, Exclude becomes None, but Refuse always stays Refuse (F1, Q-182). Added StoreDisplayPath for notices and WorkaroundId. The old Precaution text is gone.
EnabledWorkarounds (IReadOnlySet<string>, defaulting to KnownWorkarounds.DefaultEnabled) replaces Precautions.
The public overload now takes the enabled ids. Resolve is always called and receives the enabled ids. The refusal and each skipped store carry the precaution's id. The doc comment is updated.
Added NotScannedFolder.WorkaroundId and ScanResult.RefusalWorkaroundId, so the App can word notices generically. Comments no longer name the entry.
The InternalsVisibleTo ScanArm line is removed along with the rig (the stack line: deleted once O-003 is decided; spike #87 decided it).

The Settings window renders KnownWorkarounds generically: one checkbox each, ticked at launch, kept for the session. ConfirmTurnOffWindow is a WPF Yes/No window whose question states the consequence; No keeps the box ticked. Named parts let the hook find them.
Replaced by SettingsWindow. Its confirmation was a Win32 MessageBox that the hook could not drive.
PrecautionsButton becomes SettingsButton, which opens Settings.

The session set of enabled ids and the OnSettings handler. The refusal line, worded from the precaution the result names, says a folder at or inside the store is never scanned and the checkbox only governs scans of folders above it. The not-scanned outcome note names wcifs.sys and the Settings checkbox.
NotScannedRow carries the precaution's id. The row text reads 'size not counted: Windows container layers, skipped to avoid a leak in Windows' wcifs.sys driver; see Settings'.
The not-scanned tree note uses the same words as the row.
Schema-1 additions: workarounds [{id, on}] (renamed from precautions), core.notScanned and window.SettingsButton. Counts and ids only.

Changes to the planted-store tests:
- C-043: the planted store now has Hives, Bindings and dotnet.bcf beside a nested Files tree.
- C-044: a Layers\<id>\Files\Windows root is added.
- C-046: junction, subst and 8.3 refusal are merged into one test.
- C-047: 'Layers.' and 'Layers ' siblings are added.
- C-048: an absent store whose parent is also missing.
- C-049: the off test asserts the store is counted while a picked root is still Refused (F1).
- F4: the backstop test now uses a deny-ACL folder.
- The workaround ids are asserted.
It tested the A/B/C/VOID verdict judge, which the narrowing removed. Its completeness cases moved to PoolWatchCases.ps1, per the stack line: a case script, no Pester.

Rewritten lean, per design 10:
- -Prepare: publish, hook build, Rpre, environment record, fltmc paste check.
- -Protocol: plan line, R0, I0, 5 full, 4 cancelled and 1 closed, I1, with marks before, at exit and 10 min after.
- A per-arm guard (6 GiB over the arm's own /before, or under 3 GiB available) and guardAtStart cascades.
- -Rehearse: a 30,150-folder %TEMP% tree with triggers at 10–25% of its folders.
- -Report: completeness against the plan, then raw nets; exit 0 or 2; no verdict words.

No settle gate, drift, tolerance, pressure step, ScanArm or L/S/P arms.

Cases C-052 to C-056. C-053 to C-056 run -Report over hand-built JSONL fixtures. C-052 is a full -Protocol -Rehearse run that must read RUN COMPLETE and delete its scratch. Every fixture is checked for the absence of verdict words.
The rig is retired with O-003 decided (stack line; design 10).
As above.

The FSA_HOOK_MODE=settings driver. From the main window's Loaded class handler, before the scan starts, it presses SettingsButton, unticks the first box, answers the confirmation per FSA_HOOK_ANSWER (yes or no) and closes Settings, logging each step.
Accepts the settings mode and FSA_HOOK_ANSWER, and documents them.

obligations.how: The narrowed criterion and design 10 removed the settle gate and the idle-drift judgement from this slice. The new PoolWatch.ps1 has no gate and no drift check, so a gate looser on nonpaged than its drift check cannot occur here. R4-1 is handed to SC-128 by id in the design record's 'Not judged here' section, with its fix (one limit per pool, 3 × 2,229 B/s for nonpaged).

The guard is measured per arm, against that arm's own /before mark (6 GiB of pool, or under 3 GiB available), so one arm's growth can no longer stop the next. An arm that would start with available memory already under the floor is not started: it records guardAtStart, guardStop and cascadeFrom (the last arm the guard stopped). -Report lists it as 'not measured: guard already exceeded at start (cascade from X1)' and does not report it by its missing marks. PoolWatchCases C-056 checks this with X1 guard-stopped and X2 cascaded, and passes.

C-043: AScanAboveTheStoreStopsAtItAndCountsEverythingElse, on a planted store holding a nested Files\Windows tree with files, plus Hives, Bindings and dotnet.bcf. It asserts one skippedStores entry carrying the precaution's id, nothing counted or probed under the store, AfterFolder never firing at or under it, opensUnderExcludedStore 0, totals equal to the tree minus the store, and the store absent from Unreadable. Passed.

C-044: ARootAtOrInsideTheStoreIsRefused, with rows for the store itself, a layer, Layers\<id>\Files\Windows and a deeper folder. Each is Refused with the precaution's id, and the scan's guard made 0 calls, so there were no DirectoryReader listings. 4 of 4 rows passed. Report mode's exit 0 with outcome refused, on this PC's real store, is WindowCases X-001 (run within X-006, passed).

C-045: ARootInsideTheStoreInAnotherSpellingIsRefusedWithNoOpen (\\?\, trailing separator, lower and upper case). The string step alone refuses, with a cancelled token so that no open could decide it. Passed.

C-046: ARootThroughAJunctionIntoTheStoreIsRefused now covers a junction, a subst drive (subst.exe, unelevated) and the 8.3 short name of a folder inside the store. The 8.3 spelling is asserted when cmd's %~s gives a form distinct from the long one. Each is Refused with nothing in the store listed. Passed.

C-047: FoldersNamedLikeTheStoreElsewhereOrBesideItAreCounted now plants 'Layers.' and 'Layers ' (made through \\?\) beside Layers2, LayersBackup and an a\Layers elsewhere in the tree. All are counted (+3,700 B), only the store is skipped, and opensUnderExcludedStore is 0. Passed.

C-048: WithNoStoreTheScanIsWhatItWasBefore. Resolve with an absent store whose parent (the final-path step's anchor) is also missing, against an unrelated root, returns None without throwing. The scan matches the switch-off scan in totals, entry count and unreadable count, with no skipped store. The repro keeps its message-skip, unchanged. Passed.

C-049, built to F1's version: WithThePrecautionOffTheStoreIsCountedAndARootInsideItIsStillRefused, on a planted store only. With the switch off, the store is listed and counted (OutsideBytes + StoreBytes, and win.ini under it is an entry), with no NotScanned flag, no skippedStores and no backstop refusals. A root picked inside the store is still Refused. Defaults are on. Passed.

C-050: WindowCases X-006 runs X-001 and X-002 on this PC's real store through the published exe; neither opens anything in it.
- The refused root's OutcomeDetail names the defect, wcifs.sys and the Settings checkbox, and says that checkbox does not lift the refusal.
- The skipped store's outcome note says 'Skipped to avoid a leak in wcifs.sys…' and names the Settings checkbox.
- The report has workarounds [{wcifs-layer-store, on: true}] and core.notScanned 1.
- The tab header counts the store apart from the unreadable folders.

Passed. 'No Show in Explorer on NotScanned' is held by the code (PathOf returns an empty path) but is not asserted in this case, because the report carries no context-menu state.

C-051: WindowCases X-005 drives the new hook mode FSA_HOOK_MODE=settings over a small %TEMP% tree.
- Answer No: the box stays ticked and the report shows on:true.
- Answer Yes: the box is unticked, the report shows on:false, and the button reads 'Settings (1 off)...'.
- A fresh launch without the hook shows on:true again.

The logged question states the consequence. Passed.

C-052: PoolWatchCases -Case C-052 runs `PoolWatch.ps1 -Protocol -Rehearse` end to end: publish, hook build, a generated 30,150-folder tree, I0, 10 runs of the published app, I1. Its -Report read RUN COMPLETE (every planned arm has /before, /exit and /settled marks, and every cancel and close acted mid-scan), it was headed REHEARSAL, and the scratch was deleted ('REHEARSAL scratch deleted: True'). Passed.

C-053: on a fixture where F3 exited 70 with no report, -Report exits 2 with RUN INCOMPLETE and lists 'arm F3: a full scan that exited 70, not 0' and 'arm F3: a full scan that wrote no report'. The clean fixture reads RUN COMPLETE and exits 0. No line carries a verdict word. Passed.

C-054: when X2 is missing from arms.jsonl, -Report lists 'arm X2: in the plan but not in arms.jsonl, so it never started' and the 5-and-4 count. With no exe arm at all, it lists every arm and 'the run holds 0 full and 0 cancelled or closed exe runs, not 5 and 5'. Passed.

C-055: three fixtures, each listed with the hook's line where it has one.
- X4 (a cancel run): 'the app shut down before the trigger' (exit 70, no report).
- X2: trigger deadline passed, status Completed.
- X5 (the close run): 'the app shut down before the trigger'.
Each is listed as a run 'whose hook never acted', quoting the hook's refused line. X1, pressed but with a Completed report, is listed as 'not Cancelled'. Passed.

C-056: a missing F4/settled mark gives 'arm F4: mark F4/settled is missing'. X1, stopped by the guard, is listed with its net at the stop; X2, started over the guard, is listed as 'not measured: guard already exceeded at start (cascade from X1)' and not by its missing marks. No fixture line carries PASS, FAIL, VOID or OUTCOME. Passed.

F1, as decided:
- The switch governs only the C: exclusion and, with it, the backstop's rule. Refused stays unconditional: ContainerLayerStore.Resolve turns only an Exclude into None.
- Case 7 now asserts 'off: store listed and counted; picked root still Refused'.
- IfTurnedOff, the confirmation and the refusal line no longer promise that a picked root will be scanned.
- The design record cites where the per-bug workaround rule lives: the TAAD engine's standing build-stage rule, with no Q-number or repository file.
- Design 10's open question (should off lift the refusal?) is left with the person.

F2:
- The per-arm pool ceiling is 6 GiB over the arm's own /before. The arithmetic is in PoolWatch.ps1 and the design record: about 800 B per directory listed (spike #87: 537 MB at 669,824 listings), so about 0.7 GiB for ~920,000 folders; plus about 1 KB per first-time open of 2.35M–3.7M files, so 2.3–3.6 GiB; 3–4.4 GiB in all.
- 'Available under 3 GiB' stays as the machine protection.
- -Report prints a guard-stopped arm's net from /before to /exit.
- The claim that the guard 'can be met' is dropped; the record says the cold cost is unmeasured.

F3: I read spike #87's C:\WINDOWS\TEMP\sl095-o003-20261005-004311\L\L.json (skippedByRule 1, skippedPaths …\Containers\Layers, 0 opens under the store) and skips.log, and counted dirs.log. Containers is listed at line 23,422 of 669,824, and all 642,894 C:\Users\ and C:\Windows\ folders come after it, so L passed the store before its cutoff. The record narrows invariant 3 to 'the walk up to the guard cutoff (3,313,298 entries)', states that the tail after the cutoff and any other WCI store are unmeasured (O-049, O-084), and gives the reopen condition. L.json, skips.log and the counts are copied under docs/design/SL-095-runs/spike-87-2026-10-04/. The run's marks.jsonl and events.log are gone, which is recorded as a gap in the risk-spike stage's record.

F4: TheReaderRefusesAndCountsAFolderUnderTheStoreWithNoOpen now denies FILE_LIST_DIRECTORY on the planted store's L1\Files, so an open that was actually issued would return error 5. DirectoryReader.Read returns InsideExcludedStore (asserted to be not ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED), with 0 guard calls and OpensUnderExcludedStore = 1. A folder beside the store is listed and not counted. Passed.

F5:
- The rehearsal tree is 30,150 folders, which the app takes many 250 ms window ticks to list (X-003's measured shape). The hook probes every 50 ms.
- Folder triggers sit at 10%, 15%, 20% and 25% of the folders, and the close at 20%.
- FSA_HOOK_TRIGGER_DEADLINE_S is 120.
- When a run is incomplete, -Report's MISSING lines quote the hook's refused line, and PoolWatchCases echoes them, so a timing loss can be told apart from a harness defect.

The unattended rehearsal read RUN COMPLETE.

deviations:
Design 10 was written against afd021d and assumed nothing existed, so it said 'build new'. Attempts 2–5 had already built most of the scanner change under other names. I adapted that code instead of writing it again:
- Workarounds/WorkaroundSwitches became KnownWorkarounds plus ScanOptions.EnabledWorkarounds.
- Id 'wcifs-container-layers' became 'wcifs-layer-store'.
- PrecautionsWindow became SettingsWindow.
- The report field precautions became workarounds.

PoolWatch was rewritten lean as the design says. ScanArm and the old verdict xUnit tests were deleted.

Case 7 (C-049) and the design's key decision both said the off position also scans a picked root inside the store. I built critique-4's accepted F1 instead: the switch governs only the exclusion, and the refusal stays unconditional, as Q-182 decided. The design's open question about this stays with the person.

The machine guard's pool ceiling is 6 GiB of growth over the arm's own /before, not the 2 GiB design 10 set. F2 (accepted) showed that 2 GiB would cut off the first cold full scan (predicted 3–4.4 GiB, arithmetic in the record). The 3 GiB Available floor is as designed.

The four new architecture rules stay SETTLED entries under '# settled by SL-095', where the engine appended them, with fire and quiet plants (S30–S38, all AS-RECORDED). They are not twinned with xUnit Facts, and the RuleCases pins are not edited, as design 10's key decision asked. In this repo every engine-appended rule since SL-023 is settled, and the fitness.yaml header defines a twinned entry as one above the first marker with a Fact. Moving engine-written entries and adding Facts would be a change to the rule mechanism this design did not argue for.

The rehearsal uses 30 s idle windows, marks every 5 s and /settled 15 s after exit, not the 60 s / 30 s the design named. This keeps the unattended validate run near five minutes; it measures completeness, not pool.

An arm whose /before already finds Available under the guard is not started (guardAtStart, cascadeFrom). The design said such an arm would start and be killed at its first poll. Not starting it spares the machine, and -Report names it as the cascade either way.

-Protocol -Rehearse runs the -Prepare steps itself (publish and hook build) into its scratch folder, so it runs unattended at validate with no person-run -Prepare first. Design 10 did not say where the rehearsal's binaries come from.

The Settings window is built in code (src/FsAnalyser.App/SettingsWindow.cs, following the old PrecautionsWindow), not as SettingsWindow.xaml. KnownWorkaround also carries a Title field (the checkbox label) beside the design's fields.
core.notScanned is added under the design's name beside the existing core.skippedStores, which holds the same count, so X-002, X-004 and read-window keep working.
Design 10's rehearsal tree was 'about 2,000 folders and 10,000 files'. Per F5 (accepted) it is 30,150 folders, so the folder-count triggers act mid-scan rather than losing the race to the scan's end.
not_built: xUnit twins for the four new rules, and the RuleCases pin edits design 10 asked for: kept as settled rules (see deviations).

A window-case assertion that the NotScanned row offers no 'Show in Explorer'. The code holds it (PathOf returns empty for NotScanned rows, unchanged since attempt 2), but the schema-1 report carries no context-menu state to assert through.
The real person-run session (-Prepare, Start > Restart, -Protocol) and the elevated `fltmc filters` paste. Both need a person; the rehearsal stands in for -Protocol's mechanics only.
follow_ups: This loop has run five laps. Build attempts 2–5 were each sent back by review findings in PoolWatch's verdict code, with the scanner change unchanged; the narrowing removed that judge. If a further lap is ordered, a person may want it limited to findings in what remains (completeness and raw nets).
Design 10's open question is for the person: should the checkbox's off position also lift the picked-root refusal (Q-182), or govern only the exclusion, as built?

Rule overlap and stale text. Four overlapping SL-095 store-spelling rules are now settled in fitness.yaml (from design laps 1, 2, 3 and 10). The settled rule 'product code never switches the per-file metadata probe off' still names tests/window/ScanArm, which is now deleted, in its `because` text. Rule text is engine-written; tidying it is a candidate.

The real session's cold cost per exe arm is unmeasured. If the 6 GiB per-arm guard still stops the first cold full scan, -Report lists that arm as incomplete with its net at the stop. SC-128 should set the ceiling from that figure.

architecture.find: a panel for unreadable folders and the coverage gap,
architecture.replace: a panel for unreadable folders, the folders left out on purpose (the container layer store, which offers no 'open in Explorer') and the coverage gap, a Settings window listing each workaround for a defect outside the app (Core's KnownWorkarounds) with its own checkbox (on at every launch, kept for the session; turning one off asks first, in a confirmation window that states the consequence), a 'Not scanned' ending when a picked root is refused, saying why,
architecture.why: src/FsAnalyser.App/SettingsWindow.cs (SettingsWindow and ConfirmTurnOffWindow), MainWindow.xaml's SettingsButton and OnSettings, and UnreadableRows.NotScannedRow, with PathOf giving it no Explorer path. WindowCases X-005 and X-006 passed. This replaces attempt 2's AA-008 text, which named a Precautions window.

architecture.find: It records every folder it could not open instead of dropping it silently.
architecture.replace: It records every folder it could not open instead of dropping it silently. It never lists the Windows container layer store (%ProgramData%\Microsoft\Windows\Containers\Layers) or anything in it, and it finds the store by path, not by attributes, once per scan before anything is listed. A root at or inside the store is refused with nothing listed or probed, whatever the settings say. While the precaution against wcifs.sys's leak (microsoft/Windows-Containers#646) is on, as it is unless the person turns it off, a scan above the store records it as one folder not scanned and never opened, its size not counted and kept apart from the unreadable folders. Only a root that reaches the store under another spelling, such as a junction or subst drive, is opened once to find its final path.
architecture.why: src/FsAnalyser.Core/Scanning/ContainerLayerStore.cs Resolve: Refuse is never cleared, and only Exclude becomes None when 'wcifs-layer-store' is off. Scanner.Scan/FolderDone and DirectoryReader.Read's backstop. Shown by ContainerLayerStoreTests.WithThePrecautionOffTheStoreIsCountedAndARootInsideItIsStillRefused and ARootAtOrInsideTheStoreIsRefused (passed) and by the repro (exit 0). This replaces AA-007's text, which tied the refusal to the switch.
